title: When People Ate Mummies as Medicine
style: Stylized realistic 3D CGI animation still, high-end animated explainer look, Pixar-meets-realism, cinematic soft lighting, detailed skin, hair and fabric, expressive faces, shallow depth of field, no text, no letters, no gore, vertical 9:16 framing.

sections.name: When People Ate Mummies as Medicine

lines.prompt: An Egyptian tomb lit by torches, an explorer in 1600s clothing lifting a wrapped mummy from a stone sarcophagus

lines: For hundreds of years, Europeans ate dead people as medicine. Specifically, Egyptian mummies.

lines.prompt: A 1600s apothecary grinding dark brown powder with a mortar and pestle, jars on shelves behind him

lines: Mummies were ground into a powder called mumia, and sold in apothecary shops.

lines.prompt: A wealthy 1600s nobleman in a ruff collar stirring brown powder into a goblet of wine, looking pleased

lines: People mixed it into drinks to treat bruises, headaches and almost anything else.

lines.prompt: A dusty Egyptian chamber with a jar of black sticky resin, a scholar reading an old scroll

lines: It may have started with a translation mix up. Mumia was originally a word for a natural black tar used as medicine.

lines.prompt: A shady merchant at night wrapping a fresh body in bandages in a back alley warehouse, lantern light, comedic sneaky expression

lines: Demand got so high that some sellers made fake mummies from recently dead bodies.

lines.prompt: A modern museum gallery, visitors looking respectfully at a mummy in a glass case

lines: The trend only faded in the 1700s. Today, mummies go to museums instead of medicine cabinets.
